title: The Six Trigonometric Functions
seo_title: Six Trigonometric Functions Worksheet: Reference Angles and Exact Values | 100 Questions
standard_text: Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4 and π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π−x, π+x, and 2π−x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on the six trigonometric functions: reference angles, exact values in all quadrants, secant, cosecant, cotangent and points on a circle. 100 questions.
key_big: Find the value for the reference angle, then take the sign from the quadrant.
body_html:
How it works

  • For a point (x, y) on the terminal side at distance r from the origin: sin θ = y/r, cos θ = x/r, tan θ = y/x.
  • The reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.
  • The reference angle is the acute angle to the x-axis. Find the value for the reference angle, then choose the sign from the quadrant.
  • Signs: all positive in Quadrant I, sine (and csc) positive in II, tangent (and cot) positive in III, cosine (and sec) positive in IV.
Example

Find cos 240°.

Quadrant III, reference angle 240° − 180° = 60°

cos 60° = 12, and cosine is negative in III

Answer: −12

Example

If sin θ = 35 and θ is in Quadrant II, find tan θ.

y = 3, r = 5, so |x| = 4

In Quadrant II, x = −4

tan θ = 3/(−4)

Answer: −34

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the sign from the quadrant.
  • Taking sec as 1/sin. sec goes with cos, csc goes with sin.
  • Measuring the reference angle to the y-axis. Always use the x-axis.
  • Mixing up sine and cosine: cosine is the x-coordinate, sine is the y-coordinate.

faq.q: What are the six trigonometric functions?
faq.a: Sine, cosine and tangent, and their reciprocals cosecant, secant and cotangent.

faq.q: How do you find a reference angle?
faq.a: Find the acute angle between the terminal side and the x-axis: 180° − θ in Quadrant II, θ − 180° in Quadrant III and 360° − θ in Quadrant IV.

faq.q: How do I remember which functions are positive?
faq.a: All are positive in Quadrant I, sine in II, tangent in III and cosine in IV. Some students say All Students Take Calculus.

faq.q: When is a trigonometric function undefined?
faq.a: When its denominator is 0. For example, tan 90° and sec 90° are undefined because cos 90° = 0.

sets.title: Points on a circle and applications

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a radius of 20 ft, and its center is 25 ft above the ground. A seat starts level with the center on the right and turns 150° counterclockwise. To the nearest foot, how high is the seat?
items.e: Height = center + r sin θ = 25 + 20 sin 150° ≈ 25 + 10.0 ≈ 35 ft.

items.q: A point moves counterclockwise around a circle of radius 4 centered at the origin, starting at (4, 0). Where is it after turning 5π3?
items.e: The point is (r cos θ, r sin θ) = (4 · 12, 4 · (−√32)) = (2, −2√3).

items.q: A point moves counterclockwise around a circle of radius 2 centered at the origin, starting at (2, 0). Where is it after turning 4π3?
items.e: The point is (r cos θ, r sin θ) = (2 · (−12), 2 · (−√32)) = (−1, −√3).

items.q: The point (20, 21) is on the terminal side of an angle θ in standard position. What is cos θ?
items.e: r = √(20² + 21²) = 29. Then sin = y/r, cos = x/r, tan = y/x and the reciprocals. cos θ = 2029.
